title: AEOeye vs Nightwatch: AI Visibility Tracking Compared (2026)
metaTitle: Nightwatch vs AEOeye: AI Visibility Tracking Compared
metaDescription: What Nightwatch's AI tracking does, what it costs as of October 2026, and when AEOeye or a dedicated AI visibility tracker is the better choice.
shortAnswer: Nightwatch is an SEO rank tracker, with ranking history back to 2012, that now also tracks how AI answers mention your brand. It fits teams that already pay for keyword tracking. AEOeye does a different job: a one-time audit of whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity name you. Choose Nightwatch for daily SEO-plus-AI monitoring, AEOeye for a first snapshot, and a dedicated tracker when prompt depth matters most.
intro:
This guide rests on Nightwatch's public documentation (pricing page, product pages and help docs) as of 3 October 2026; we have not tested Nightwatch hands-on. AEOeye is our product, so we say plainly where Nightwatch is the better pick.

Most visitors arrive after searching "nightwatch seo" or "nightwatch io". They want to know what it is, what its AI tracking does, and whether a dedicated tool would do the job better. We answer from Nightwatch's own pages, not from review sites.

sections.heading: What is Nightwatch, and is it an SEO tool or an AI visibility tool?
sections.body:
Nightwatch is an SEO rank tracker that added AI visibility tracking. Its [homepage](https://nightwatch.io/) describes daily positions on Google, Bing, YouTube, DuckDuckGo and Yahoo, rank history stored since 2012, and checks from 107,000+ locations in 190+ countries.

The AI module sits inside that product, next to keyword research, a site audit, white-label reports and an SEO agent. Plans are priced by keywords tracked (500, 2,500 or 7,500), with AI prompts as a second allowance, per the [pricing page](https://nightwatch.io/pricing/). That shape suits an SEO team and fits badly if you only want AI answers.

When we checked Nightwatch's own site for [AEOeye's crawler access study](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory) on 3 October 2026, its robots.txt blocked none of the AI crawlers we tested and named none, and /llms.txt returned a 404. The served homepage HTML carried FAQPage, SoftwareApplication, Offer and AggregateRating schema but no Organization type (schema injected by JavaScript would not show in our fetch). That is a fact box, not a verdict on the product.

sections.heading: What does Nightwatch's AI visibility tracking actually do?
sections.body:
Nightwatch asks AI platforms the prompts you supply, on a schedule, and reports whether and where your brand appears. Per its [help docs](https://docs.nightwatch.io/en/articles/13842311-ai-llm-tracking-in-nightwatch), each prompt gets a provider, country and language, and results list detected brands, position, sentiment and cited domains. The default refresh is daily.

Dashboards cover visibility, share of voice, sentiment, cited sources and a Source Matrix that the docs label beta. Nightwatch's [AI share-of-voice guide](https://nightwatch.io/blog/ai-share-of-voice/) defines share of voice as your brand mentions divided by all brand mentions across tracked prompts. The idea comes from advertising, where [share of voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Share_of_voice) measures one company's slice of category spending.

The headline feature is Citation Intelligence, which joins ranking changes to AI citation changes. Its premise, stated on the [AI tracking page](https://nightwatch.io/ai-tracking/), is that ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity cite what ranks on Google. We think that is half true. Nightwatch's own blog says the overlap is real but "not a direct one-to-one relationship", and that ChatGPT and Perplexity regularly surface lower-ranking pages.

Google says AI Overviews and AI Mode may use [query fan-out](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) and show a wider, more diverse set of links than classic search. A [University of Toronto study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08919) found AI search leans heavily toward earned media over brand-owned content. So the rank-to-citation link is most useful for Google's own AI surfaces; for ChatGPT or Claude recommendations, whether third-party sources name you matters at least as much.

![Overhead view of laptops, charts and printed reports spread across a desk for data analysis](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8062289/pexels-photo-8062289.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do Nightwatch and AEOeye compare?
sections.body:
They answer different questions. Nightwatch monitors a fixed prompt set every day inside an SEO subscription. AEOeye runs a one-time audit of the questions buyers ask and shows the real answers. AEOeye is not a daily tracker and does not pretend to be.

- **Free start:** AEOeye's [free audit](/) asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions live and shows the answers in full, plus the competitors AI recommends instead. Nightwatch offers a 14-day trial on every plan.
- **Engines:** the $29 AEOeye full report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity and ten questions, each engine at the default tier a free user sees. Nightwatch's engine list varies by page (see below).
- **Price basis:** AEOeye is $0 or $29 once, with no subscription. Nightwatch starts at €99 a month (€79 billed yearly) as of October 2026.
- **Setup:** AEOeye needs a brand name. Nightwatch needs a domain, keywords and a prompt list.

Nightwatch's own pages disagree on engines. The pricing page lists ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Mode and AI Overview on every plan. The AI tracking page's FAQ names Microsoft Copilot and does not mention AI Mode or AI Overview, and a help article dated 27 February 2026 omits Claude and reserves Gemini for plans with 300+ prompts. Confirm in the trial what your plan runs.

sections.heading: When is an SEO rank tracker with an AI add-on enough?
sections.body:
It is enough when rank tracking is already a paid, ongoing job. Then AI prompts come inside the plan, there are no per-seat fees, and Citation Intelligence puts rankings and AI answers in one report. For agencies that is a real saving over a second subscription.

On the [pricing page](https://nightwatch.io/pricing/), Starter includes 50 AI prompts, Professional 150 and Agency 500, with white-label reports and Looker Studio from Professional. Monthly billing is €99, €199 and €499; yearly billing brings those to €79, €159 and €399 a month. Older write-ups, including an earlier version of this page, described a separate AI add-on of about $99 a month. The current pricing page shows none, so treat that figure as outdated.

For a price-and-value view, see [is Nightwatch AI tracking worth the price](/answers/nightwatch-ai-tracking-price-worth-it).

![A person reviewing business data with colorful graphs on a tablet screen](https://images.pexels.com/photos/36950598/pexels-photo-36950598.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: When do you need a dedicated AI visibility tool?
sections.body:
You need one when AI answers are the whole job: many prompts, many engines, and enough repeat runs to trust the numbers. That is where Nightwatch's allowance is thinnest, because answers vary from run to run.

SparkToro, working with Gumshoe.ai, had 600 volunteers run 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google's AI a combined 2,961 times in [late 2025](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/). There was under a 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice from ChatGPT or Google's AI. They suggest 60 to 100 runs per prompt and treat visibility percentage, not position, as the usable metric.

Nightwatch's Starter plan allows 1,500 AI answers a month for 50 prompts, which is our arithmetic for 30 per prompt. Because the docs set one provider per prompt, we read that as one engine, once a day. Check whether a prompt counts once per engine before you budget.

| Entry plan (3 Oct 2026) | Price | Prompts | AI answers a month |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nightwatch Starter | €99/mo (€79 yearly) | 50 | 1,500 |
| [Peec AI Starter](https://peec.ai/pricing) | $95/mo | 50, any 3 models | 4,500 |
| [Otterly Lite](https://otterly.ai/pricing) | $29/mo | 15, 4 engines | not stated |
| Otterly Standard | $189/mo | 100, 4 engines | not stated |

Peec defines monthly answers as prompts times active models times frequency. Entry prices per prompt sit in the same range across these tools; the difference is sampling depth. Compare options in our [AI visibility tracker roundup](/blog/ai-visibility-tracker) and [best AI visibility tools](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools).

sections.heading: Which should you choose?
sections.body:
Choose by the job you have today, not by the logo. Run a snapshot first if you have never seen what AI says about you, because the snapshot tells you whether you have a presence problem or a measurement problem.

1. **You already pay for rank tracking, or run an agency:** start Nightwatch's trial. Test Citation Intelligence on keywords you rank for, and check the engines and answers per prompt.
2. **You need to know today whether AI names you:** run the [free AEOeye audit](/), then the $29 report for five engines and ten questions. No subscription.
3. **You need hundreds of prompts and deep sampling:** use a dedicated tracker, or see the [Nightwatch alternatives](/alternatives/nightwatch).

Many teams do 2 then 1: snapshot first, then a monitoring subscription once the numbers justify it.

![Close-up of an antique apothecary scale beside pill bottles in a vintage pharmacy](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8657361/pexels-photo-8657361.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

keyTakeaways: Nightwatch is an SEO rank tracker first; AI tracking is one module on plans priced by keywords tracked.
As of October 2026 AI prompts are included on every plan (50, 150, 500), not a separate add-on.
Its Starter allowance works out to 30 answers per prompt a month, well short of the 60 to 100 runs SparkToro suggests.
Nightwatch's pages disagree on which AI engines are covered, so confirm during the trial.
AEOeye is a one-time audit, not a daily tracker: free on ChatGPT, $29 for five engines.

faqs.a: Nightwatch is an SEO rank tracker. It checks keyword positions daily on Google, Bing, YouTube, DuckDuckGo and Yahoo, keeps history back to 2012, and now adds AI visibility tracking across ChatGPT and other AI platforms. Plans are priced by keywords tracked and include unlimited team seats.

faqs.q: How much does Nightwatch AI tracking cost?
faqs.a: As of 3 October 2026, Starter is €99 a month (€79 billed yearly) with 50 AI prompts, Professional €199 (€159 yearly) with 150, and Agency €499 (€399 yearly) with 500. AI prompts are included in each plan; Enterprise is custom-priced. Its pricing page quotes euros and offers a 14-day trial.

faqs.q: Which AI engines does Nightwatch track?
faqs.a: It depends on the page. The pricing page lists ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Mode and AI Overview; the AI tracking page FAQ names Microsoft Copilot but not the Google surfaces; a February 2026 help article omits Claude. Confirm which engines your plan actually runs during the free trial before committing.

faqs.q: Is there a free way to check my AI visibility before paying?
faqs.a: Yes. AEOeye's free audit asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions live and shows the real answers and the competitors AI recommends instead. Nightwatch offers a 14-day trial instead of a free plan, and it warns that it bills automatically if you do not cancel within 14 days.

faqs.q: Should I use Nightwatch or a dedicated AI visibility tool?
faqs.a: Use Nightwatch if rank tracking is already a paid job and you want AI answers in the same report. Use a dedicated tracker if you need many prompts and repeat runs per prompt. Run a free AEOeye snapshot first if you have never seen what AI says about your brand.
